tests/test_analyze.py.title: Relationship analysis
tests/test_analyze.py.description: Statistical behaviour of the analysis: finds real effects, ignores noise, reads the CSV files.

tests/test_autosync.py.title: Automatic sync when the dashboard opens
tests/test_autosync.py.description:
GitHub often starts the scheduled sync hours late. The dashboard starts it itself when it opens
after 08:00 and the last sync is from before today, at most once in 3 hours, and pauses for a
week when the token may not start workflows. The helper runs in Node; without Node these tests
are skipped.

tests/test_bloodpressure.py.title: Blood pressure
tests/test_bloodpressure.py.description: Parsing Garmin's nested response and replacing the stored window.

tests/test_climbs.py.title: Bouldering
tests/test_climbs.py.description: Climbing splits: parsing, self evaluation and which sessions a sync fetches again.

tests/test_config.py.title: Settings
tests/test_config.py.description: settings.json and the time zone: missing, broken and valid files, and which source wins.

tests/test_dashboard.py.title: Dashboard
tests/test_dashboard.py.description: The English dictionary in dashboard/index.html covers every text the script translates.

tests/test_energy.py.title: Energy expenditure from measured values
tests/test_energy.py.description:
A resting metabolic rate measured by indirect calorimetry (Befunde → Ruheumsatz) replaces Garmin's
resting kcal (total minus active) from the day of the measurement until the next one, as a factor
on Garmin's value or as the measured value itself. Garmin's columns stay unchanged, and with the
mode off nothing changes. The dashboard (JavaScript) and the recommendations (selftopo/energy.py)
follow the same rules; the dashboard half runs in Node and is skipped without it.

tests/test_energy_dashboard.py.title: Energy expenditure in the dashboard: settings, texts and charts
tests/test_energy_dashboard.py.description:
Settings → General → Energy expenditure chooses how a measured RMR is used and shows the factor with
what it rests on. The helpers run in Node; without Node these tests are skipped.

tests/test_fitness.py.title: Fitness metrics
tests/test_fitness.py.description: Garmin fitness metrics: parsing the endpoints and merging the window into the CSV.

tests/test_lifestyle.py.title: Lifestyle Logging
tests/test_lifestyle.py.description:
Parsing Garmin's daily log and fetching day by day. The response shape is assumed (see
selftopo/lifestyle.py), so these tests pin the mapping, not Garmin's real answer.

tests/test_measurements.py.title: Befunde: measurements.csv
tests/test_measurements.py.description:
Values from labs and tests entered in the dashboard. Rows are read leniently but never guessed:
a row without a date, a number or a known kind is counted as unreadable. The card shows the
newest value per measure, a RER next to the resting metabolic rate of the same day, and rates
blood values only against the reference range on the report. The helpers run in Node; without
Node these tests are skipped.

tests/test_navigation.py.title: Where the dashboard opens
tests/test_navigation.py.description:
The page opens at the overview. A link opened fresh (#kraft) jumps to its area; a reload ignores
both the area in the address and the old scroll position. Runs the page's own startPosition in Node
with a stand-in browser; without Node these tests are skipped.

tests/test_overview.py.title: Overview tiles and time range
tests/test_overview.py.description:
Weight coloured by BMI, calories by energy balance, tiles filled by state with a summary above
them (design D), and the one-week range. The helpers run in Node; without Node these tests are
skipped.

tests/test_parsers.py.title: Garmin and Hevy parsers
tests/test_parsers.py.description: Mapping of Garmin and Hevy responses to CSV rows, and the Garmin login in the workflow.

tests/test_push.py.title: Push notifications
tests/test_push.py.description:
The Today card as a Web Push message: keys, the text in German and English, which subscriptions
count, what happens with expired ones, and that nothing is sent without the secret or without a
Today card for today. Sending itself is replaced by a stand-in; no message leaves the test.

tests/test_recommend.py.title: Recommendations
tests/test_recommend.py.description:
Goals from settings.json, the rules of the recommendation catalogue with their safety limits,
goal forecasts and experiments. Each test writes a small, made-up data set and checks which cards
come out.

tests/test_recommend_dashboard.py.title: Recommendations in the dashboard
tests/test_recommend_dashboard.py.description:
The Today card computed in the browser, the texts from recommendations.json and the goals in
settings.json as the page reads them. The helpers run in Node; without Node these tests are
skipped. Every German text the Python rules write has an English translation.

tests/test_release.py.title: Releases from the changelog
tests/test_release.py.description:
tools/release.py tags every version of CHANGELOG.md on the squash commit of its pull request and
publishes it as a GitHub release; the workflow Release runs it after the tests pass on main.

tests/test_reports.py.title: Reports read by the Claude API
tests/test_reports.py.description:
Files in files/ that no row of measurements.csv points to go to the Claude API once; what it finds
becomes rows with status `proposed`, values outside the plausible range or without a valid date are
dropped, and report_evaluations.json keeps every file from being sent twice. The API is faked here.

tests/test_save_settings.py.title: Saving settings from the dashboard
tests/test_save_settings.py.description:
With a token that may write ("Contents: Read and write"), "Save" commits settings.json to the data
repository through the GitHub API. The page's own writeSettings runs in Node against a stand-in
for GitHub; without Node these tests are skipped.

tests/test_sleepdebt.py.title: Sleep debt
tests/test_sleepdebt.py.description:
The last four nights against the sleep need (goal or 8 hours): shortfalls add up, a longer night
pays back, never below zero; old nights do not count. The helper runs in Node; without Node these
tests are skipped.

tests/test_sync_dashboard.py.title: When the data was fetched, as the dashboard shows it
tests/test_sync_dashboard.py.description:
The header names the time of the last sync from sync_status.json, not only when the page loaded.
It turns yellow after 30 hours, names sources that failed, and offers the run on GitHub. The
helpers run in Node; without Node these tests are skipped.

tests/test_syncstatus.py.title: Sync status
tests/test_syncstatus.py.description:
data/sync_status.json: when the last sync ran, how it was started and how each source did, so the
dashboard can tell fresh data from a late or failed run.

tests/test_ui.py.title: Dashboard layout, accessibility and wording
tests/test_ui.py.description:
Acceptance criteria of the UI stories that are fixed in the markup, the stylesheet or small
helpers: landmarks and the skip link, text and touch-target sizes, the tile grid, series colours
that never look like a verdict, collapsed areas, and the wording of notices. Read from
dashboard/index.html; the helpers run in Node, without Node those tests are skipped.

tests/test_versions.py.title: One version per change
tests/test_versions.py.description:
Every change gets a semantic version: the newest entry in CHANGELOG.md, selftopo.__version__ and
APP_VERSION in the dashboard are the same number, versions only go up, and each one says what
changed.

tests/test_yazio.py.title: YAZIO
tests/test_yazio.py.description: Parsing the daily summary, token handling and the replace-the-window sync.

tests.name: test_finds_an_injected_next_night_effect_with_the_right_size
tests.title: Finds an injected next night effect with the right size
tests.doc:
200 synthetic days in which every training-load point lowers the next night's HRV by 0.04 ms.

The analysis must mark load → HRV one night later as robust, estimate about −4 ms per 100 load
points, and must not report the same effect two nights later.

inputs.name: injected_effect
inputs.value: '-0.04 ms HRV per load point, the following night'

tests.name: test_false_alarm_rate_on_pure_noise_stays_near_the_fdr_level
tests.title: False alarm rate on pure noise stays near the fdr level
tests.doc:
On 40 data sets of pure noise, at most 20 % of the runs may report any robust finding.

With Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.10 about 1 run in 10 is expected; clearly more would mean the
dashboard presents chance as an insight.

inputs.name: data
inputs.value: '200 random days each, no real effect'

tests.name: test_circular_garmin_pairs_are_not_tested
tests.title: Circular garmin pairs are not tested
tests.doc:
Pairs in which Garmin derives one value from the other are not tested.

Sleep score → Training Readiness and stress → Body Battery correlate by construction, so a
finding there would say nothing. Bedtime → readiness is a real question and stays in.

tests.name: test_endpoints_are_parsed_per_day
tests.title: Endpoints are parsed per day
tests.doc:
VO2max, race predictions, Hill Score and Endurance Score become one value per day.

VO2max is rounded to one decimal, race times stay in seconds, days without a value are dropped,
and the Endurance Score combines the weekly averages with today's value.

tests.name: test_status_of_the_primary_device
tests.title: Status of the primary device
tests.doc:
Training status, loads and ACWR come from the primary device; fitness age to one decimal.

The Endurance Score limits are kept for the gauge; a missing load balance stays empty.

tests.name: test_sync_replaces_the_window_and_writes_today
tests.title: Sync replaces the window and writes today
tests.doc:
A 30-day sync replaces the stored window, keeps older rows and writes today's status.

A day Garmin no longer reports is dropped; a failed endpoint (here Hill Score) leaves its
columns empty instead of stopping the sync.
